summary: Today’s pulse tracks Protests under way in Germany and France as minister warns against use of Halloween masks – Europe live, Almost 50 arrested at protest against Palestine Action ban outside US embassy in London, and Crypto firm Binance covers 90% of losses after $6.3bn hack. Across Guardian and BBC, the strongest repeated signals are early, people, and votes. In the background, More than 50m Americans cast ballots in early voting with three days to go before midterms and Ukrainian evacuees reunite with family after years trapped in Russia-occupied city keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: Protests under way in Germany and France as minister warns against use of Halloween masks – Europe live
headlines.description: France’s interior minister, Laurent Nuñez, has warned protesters that covering their faces with Halloween costumes could result in fines Protesters in Paris have begun marching from Porte de Bagnolet, with demonstrations also taking place in Lille and Lyon . Crowds of people have gathered in Paris for the protests, where two French student unions have called for a blockade of schools and universities on Tuesday and Thursday.

headlines.title: Almost 50 arrested at protest against Palestine Action ban outside US embassy in London
headlines.description: Met alleges demonstrators ‘meeting to purposefully commit a crime’ in first such gathering under Burnham Almost 50 people have been arrested at the first mass demonstrations under Andy Burnham’s premiership opposing the proscription of Palestine Action. Hundreds of people gathered outside the US embassy in Battersea, south London, holding signs that read: “I oppose genocide, I support Palestine Action.” Demonstrators also held a vigil in support of the group outside the US consulate in Edinburgh.

headlines.title: Crypto firm Binance covers 90% of losses after $6.3bn hack
headlines.description: Two analytics firms say they have robust intelligence pointing to a North Korean state-backed group as the likely culprit.

headlines.title: More than 50m Americans cast ballots in early voting with three days to go before midterms
headlines.description: Record number of early votes cast, with Democrats outnumbering Republicans in states which collect that information There has been a surge of early voting for the US midterm elections, with millions more Americans going to the polls compared with the last such election amid a series of tight contests that will determine control of Congress. More than 50.5m early votes have been cast across the US as of Saturday morning, according to an analysis by the University of Florida . This is already nearly 5m more votes than the total number of early votes made in the last midterm elections, in 2022.

headlines.title: Ukrainian evacuees reunite with family after years trapped in Russia-occupied city
headlines.description: Oleshky residents had been without food, water and electricity, with many resorting to cooking garden weeds to survive.

headlines.description: Government data shows that more than 10,000 people have contracted the rare virus.

headlinePool.title: UK charity shop profits plummet amid shift in secondhand clothes market
headlinePool.description: British Heart Foundation describes ‘exceptionally challenging’ trading after Oxfam’s retail profit reportedly fell 23% amid rise of platforms such as Vinted Profits at some of the UK’s best-known charity shops have plummeted as they face a number of pressures, including from online secondhand clothes platforms, prompting claims that a key part of the sector’s fundraising model could be under threat. According to unpublished accounts seen by the Financial Times , Oxfam’s retail profit fell 23% to £4.9m in the last financial year, compared with £6.4m in the previous year.

headlinePool.title: A world-first focus on long-term outcomes could transform UK government – or create new spending fights
headlinePool.description: Tucked away in John Healey’s budget is decision to ringfence preventative projects where future savings outweigh initial cost It merited the briefest of mentions in John Healey’s speech and just one paragraph in the 166-page budget document , but some believe it could revolutionise not just public spending but the very process of government itself: a new focus on long-term outcomes. The idea in the broad sense is very simple. Any spending deemed to be “preventative” – that is, the initial outlay will be more than made up for by future savings – will from now on be ringfenced, meaning it cannot be raided for more immediate needs.

headlinePool.title: Ads accusing Republican candidates of protecting Epstein fill airwaves in final midterm push
headlinePool.description: But select Democrats, too, are being accused of having ties to the late sex offender as country prepares to vote In races across the country, Democratic candidates or groups that support them have released ads accusing Republicans of protecting pedophiles by voting against legislation to release files related to Jeffrey Epstein . The ads appear intended to evoke an emotional response by accusing candidates of “protecting” Epstein, a notorious pedophile accused of running a sex-trafficking ring involving minors.

headlinePool.title: Maurene Comey ruling offers hope of check on Trump’s assault on rule of law
headlinePool.description: Legal experts welcome judge’s rejection of firing of James Comey’s daughter prosecutor but warn an appeal is likely A recent legal ruling against an effort to fire the star-prosecutor daughter of a former FBI chief targeted by Donald Trump could send a strong message about politicized firings – and influence other judges weighing similar cases, legal veterans said. Judge Jesse Furman ruled this week that the Department of Justice’s firing of assistant US attorney Maurene Comey without cause was unlawful. Comey, the daughter of former FBI director James Comey, successfully litigated numerous high-profile cases during her tenure at the southern district of New York, including guilty verdicts against Ghislaine Maxwell and Sean “Diddy” Combs.

headlinePool.title: Ethiopian PM puts ministers through military training
headlinePool.description: The prime minister has previously emphasised military preparedness as central to his government's ambitions.

headlinePool.title: Justice Department seeks to isolate Alaska ballots amid criminal probe over Senate candidate
headlinePool.description: The latest developments come amid allegations, first reported by The New York Times, that Democrats recruited a spoiler candidate in the toss-up U.S. Senate race.

headlinePool.title: Starmer says UK must get closer to Europe as US relationship changes
headlinePool.description: Shift in dealings with Washington not likely to reset once Trump leaves Oval Office, former PM says The UK and other European nations must draw closer together as the US becomes a less-reliable partner, Keir Starmer has said in his first significant political intervention since leaving No 10. The former prime minister warned European leaders of the threat posed by Russia, among others, and said the shift in relations with Washington during Donald Trump’s presidency was not likely to reset once he leaves the Oval Office. He accused them of being caught out by these new realities twice already.

headlinePool.title: UK police should not have let US force take over airbase trial, MoD documents show
headlinePool.description: According to documents obtained by the Guardian, officials accused Cambridgeshire force of breaching US-UK deal by handing over case of woman strangled by US pilot Ministry of Defence officials have privately accused a UK police force of wrongly handing over the investigation of an American fighter pilot who strangled a British woman to the US military, according to documents obtained by the Guardian. Cambridgeshire police allowed the US military police to quickly take control of the investigation into Capt Jacob Wulfson after he had been accused of sexually assaulting Sarah Steele in his Cambridge flat.

headlinePool.title: Watch: Blood donors get a Halloween fright in Thailand
headlinePool.description: Thai Red Cross workers dressed up as part of a Halloween-themed blood drive in the country's capital Bangkok.
